title: Cold rebuild: Assemble the start command
summary: Rebuild Assemble the start command from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Assemble the start command** in *CMD versus ENTRYPOINT*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The image `greeter2` was built from `CMD ["echo", "hello"]`. What happens with `docker run --rm greeter2 world`?
options: Docker tries to run a program called `world` and fails: `executable file not found`
steps.explain: With only CMD, run arguments replace the whole command, so `world` becomes the program to execute.

steps.title: Rebuild Assemble the start command cold
prompt: Write `string FinalCommand(string? entrypoint, string? cmd, string runArgs)`.
- `entrypoint` and `cmd` are exec-form JSON arrays like `["dotnet", "Api.dll"]`, or `null` when the Dockerfile does not set them.
- `runArgs` is what the user typed after the image name, space-separated, or `""`.
The result is the entrypoint's items, followed by the run arguments if there are any, otherwise the CMD's items, all joined by single spaces. If that is empty, return `error: no command specified`.
A helper `List<string> ParseArray(string? json)` that strips `[` `]`, splits on `,` and trims spaces and quotes is enough; no JSON library needed.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
string FinalCommand(string? entrypoint, string? cmd, string runArgs)
